# Security Audit - Global Context

## Scope Definition

### In Scope
- All PHP source code in app/code/Magento/ (221 modules, 10650+ files)
- Framework core in lib/internal/Magento/Framework/
- Setup code in setup/src/
- Configuration files (nginx, routes.xml, webapi.xml, di.xml)
- JavaScript/RequireJS frontend code
- GraphQL schema and resolvers

### Out of Scope
- Third-party vendor/ dependencies (beyond known CVEs)
- Test files (excluded per config)
- node_modules, dist, build directories

### Attack Surface Priority

| Priority | Description | Examples |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Critical | Internet-facing, unauthenticated | GraphQL (open-by-default), Frontend controllers, REST anonymous endpoints |
| High | Internet-facing, authenticated | Customer dashboard, REST authenticated APIs |
| Medium | Internal, authenticated | Admin panel (auth-by-default), Admin REST APIs |
| Low | Admin-only, localhost | CLI commands, Cron jobs, Setup wizards |

## Project Overview

**Application Name:** Magento 2 (Open Source / Community Edition)
**Purpose:** Full-stack e-commerce platform for online retail
**Technology Stack:** PHP 8.3+, MySQL, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, RabbitMQ, GraphQL
**Repository:** magento/magento2ce (2.4-develop branch)

## Architecture Summary

### Directory Structure
```
app/code/Magento/       # 221 modules (main application code)
lib/internal/Magento/   # Framework core (88+ subdirectories)
setup/src/              # Installation and setup code
pub/                    # Public web root
bin/                    # CLI entry point (bin/magento)
dev/                    # Development tools
phpserver/              # Built-in PHP server config
```

### Key Components
- **Entry Points:** Frontend controllers (~337), Admin controllers (~894), REST API (73 webapi.xml), GraphQL resolvers (~403), CLI commands, Cron jobs
- **Database Layer:** PDO/MySQL with ORM abstraction, QueryBuilder pattern
- **Authentication:** Multi-layer (Session + FormKey for web, Bearer Token + OAuth for API, JWT for modern API)
- **Authorization:** ACL-based RBAC with per-resource permissions

### Trust Boundaries
- Storefront <-> Frontend controllers (Session + CSRF FormKey)
- Admin panel <-> Adminhtml controllers (Admin session + ACL + SecretKey)
- API clients <-> REST/SOAP (Bearer Token/OAuth/Guest + ACL per webapi.xml resource)
- API clients <-> GraphQL (Bearer Token/Guest, per-resolver auth)

## Data Flow

### User Input Sources
- HTTP request parameters (GET/POST), headers, cookies
- REST API JSON/XML bodies
- GraphQL queries/mutations
- File uploads (images, CSV imports, theme files)
- SOAP requests
- CLI arguments (setup/admin commands)

### Sensitive Data Types
- Customer PII (name, email, address, phone)
- Payment information (credit card data via payment gateways)
- Admin credentials and tokens
- API keys and integration tokens
- Encryption keys (crypt/key config)
- Order data, pricing, inventory

### External Integrations
- Payment gateways (PayPal, CardinalCommerce/3DS)
- Shipping carriers (DHL, FedEx, UPS, USPS)
- Search engines (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch)
- Email (SMTP via Symfony Mailer)
- Analytics (Google Analytics/GTM, Adobe Analytics)
- AWS S3 (remote storage)
- RabbitMQ (async operations)
- Duo Security (2FA)

## Security-Relevant Patterns Observed

### Positive Patterns (Security Controls)
- ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD encryption (modern)
- Argon2ID13 password hashing (modern)
- CSP with nonce support (XSS prevention)
- Admin CSRF with FormKey + SecretKey
- Timing-safe comparison (Security::compareStrings)
- Session regeneration on login
- Rate limiting on password resets
- JWT token revocation mechanism
- SameSite=Lax cookies by default
- X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- HTTPOnly cookies enabled
- TRACE/TRACK HTTP methods blocked in .htaccess
- Sensitive directories (app/, setup/) denied via .htaccess
- Swagger UI disabled in production mode

### Concerning Patterns (Potential Issues)
- Frontend controllers OPEN-by-default (no auth enforcement at base class level)
- GraphQL resolvers OPEN-by-default
- 265 files with deserialization (even though using Serializer abstraction)
- 107 files with PHP magic methods (__wakeup/__destruct) - gadget chain surface
- 324 files with variable-based includes
- 104 files with weak hashing (md5/sha1) - legacy compatibility
- 49 files with predictable PRNG (rand/mt_rand/uniqid)
- Legacy encryption modes (ECB, Blowfish) still supported
- HSTS missing from nginx sample config
- Critical SQL injection taint in setup/DbValidator
- Extract() with user input found (1 file)
- preg_replace /e modifier found (1 file)
- No ReCaptcha or 2FA modules present in this codebase
- CAPTCHA per-IP threshold=1000 (effectively no IP-based rate limit)
- Admin login is case-insensitive (simplifies brute-force)
- HSTS not enabled by default
- CSP in report-only mode with unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval

### Known Sinks
- unserialize (via Serializer) - 265 files
- simplexml_load_string/DOMDocument - 15 files (XXE)
- $_FILES/move_uploaded_file - 16 files
- shell_exec/proc_open - 35 files
- eval/exec/system/passthru - 45 files
- include/require with variables - 324 files
- fputcsv - CSV injection surface
- GuzzleHttp/curl - SSRF surface

## MCP Coverage Gaps
- Pre-analysis was run (summary.json exists with rich pattern data)
- Taint correlations available for critical/high severity
- Setup code has critical SQL injection taint signals
- No MCP project loaded (MCP tools not available in this task)

## REST API Anonymous Endpoint Inventory
- 42 anonymous REST endpoints across 22 webapi.xml files
- Critical: /V1/integration/admin/token (POST) - admin credential brute-force
- Critical: /V1/integration/customer/token (POST) - customer credential brute-force
- Email enumeration: /V1/customers/isEmailAvailable (POST)
- 19+ guest cart endpoints for unauthenticated checkout flow

## GraphQL Security Notes
- 17 modules define mutations; 40 schema files total
- Auth check: context->getExtensionAttributes()->getIsCustomer()
- Query depth: 20, complexity: 1000; introspection enabled by default

     6→# SSRF Audit
     7→
     8→Systematically identify Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities that allow attackers to make the server send requests to unintended destinations.
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→SSRF occurs when an attacker can control the destination of server-side HTTP requests. This enables:
    13→- **Internal network scanning** - Discover internal services
    14→- **Cloud metadata access** - Steal AWS/GCP/Azure credentials (169.254.169.254)
    15→- **Localhost service access** - Bypass firewalls, access admin panels
    16→- **Protocol smuggling** - file://, gopher://, dict:// for RCE
    17→- **Denial of Service** - Large file downloads, slow endpoints
    18→
    19→**References:**
    20→- OWASP Top 10 A10:2021 - Server-Side Request Forgery
    21→- CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery
    22→- PortSwigger Web Security Academy: SSRF
    23→- HackerOne SSRF reports
    24→
    25→## Risk Assessment
    26→
    27→| Target | Impact | Example |
    28→|--------|--------|---------|
    29→| Cloud metadata | CRITICAL | `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/` |
    30→| Internal admin | CRITICAL | `http://localhost:8080/admin/delete-all` |
    31→| Internal services | HIGH | `http://internal-api/users` |
    32→| External with creds | HIGH | Request includes auth headers |
    33→| External arbitrary | MEDIUM | Proxy/redirect functionality |
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## Phase 0: Check Pre-Analysis Results
    38→
    39→**Pre-analysis already scanned for HTTP client sinks, URL fetching, and advanced SSRF patterns. Check those results first:**
    40→
    41→```
    42→get_pre_analysis(category="ssrf")         # HTTP clients: fetch, requests, axios, HttpClient, etc.
    43→get_pre_analysis(category="redirect")     # Redirect sinks (open redirect → SSRF chain)
    44→get_pre_analysis(category="file")         # file_get_contents can be SSRF vector
    45→
    46→get_detector_findings(category="ssrf")
    47→get_detector_findings(category="request-forgery")
    48→get_detector_findings(severity=["critical", "high"])
    49→```
    50→
    51→**For each HIGH/CRITICAL finding:**
    52→
    53→1. Validate: `validate_detector_finding(finding_id="H-001")`
    54→2. Read source: `Read("/path/to/file", offset=line-10, limit=30)`
    55→3. Check reachability: `paths_from_entries("FunctionAtLocation")`
    56→
    57→**Triage pre-analysis and detector results before moving to manual investigation. If pre-analysis data is unavailable (e.g., no MCP), skip directly to Phase 1 and use grep-based discovery instead.**

    59→---
    60→
    61→## Phase 1: Review SSRF Sinks
    62→
    63→Pre-analysis `ssrf` and `ssrf_advanced` results already located HTTP client and media processing sinks. Review those results. If pre-analysis is unavailable, or you suspect it missed sinks specific to this codebase, discover them yourself before proceeding.
    64→

    66→- Is the URL or any URL component (host, path, query params) derived from user input?
    67→- Is there URL validation before the request is made?
    68→- Can the response be read by the attacker (full SSRF) or is it blind?
    69→

    72→## Phase 2: Identify URL Sources
    73→
    74→For each HTTP sink, identify where the URL comes from:

    78→Grep("req\\.(query|params|body)\\.url", type="ts")
    79→Grep("request\\.args\\.get\\(['\"]url", type="py")
    80→Grep("\\$_GET\\[['\"]url", type="php")

name: ssrf-audit
description: Detect Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerabilities that allow attackers to make requests from the server. References OWASP A10:2021, CWE-918.
---

# SSRF Audit

Systematically identify Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities that allow attackers to make the server send requests to unintended destinations.

## Overview

SSRF occurs when an attacker can control the destination of server-side HTTP requests. This enables:
- **Internal network scanning** - Discover internal services
- **Cloud metadata access** - Steal AWS/GCP/Azure credentials (169.254.169.254)
- **Localhost service access** - Bypass firewalls, access admin panels
- **Protocol smuggling** - file://, gopher://, dict:// for RCE
- **Denial of Service** - Large file downloads, slow endpoints

**References:**
- OWASP Top 10 A10:2021 - Server-Side Request Forgery
- CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery
- PortSwigger Web Security Academy: SSRF
- HackerOne SSRF reports

## Risk Assessment

| Target | Impact | Example |
|--------|--------|---------|
| Cloud metadata | CRITICAL | `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/` |
| Internal admin | CRITICAL | `http://localhost:8080/admin/delete-all` |
| Internal services | HIGH | `http://internal-api/users` |
| External with creds | HIGH | Request includes auth headers |
| External arbitrary | MEDIUM | Proxy/redirect functionality |

---

## Phase 0: Check Pre-Analysis Results

**Pre-analysis already scanned for HTTP client sinks, URL fetching, and advanced SSRF patterns. Check those results first:**

```
get_pre_analysis(category="ssrf")         # HTTP clients: fetch, requests, axios, HttpClient, etc.
get_pre_analysis(category="redirect")     # Redirect sinks (open redirect → SSRF chain)
get_pre_analysis(category="file")         # file_get_contents can be SSRF vector

get_detector_findings(category="ssrf")
get_detector_findings(category="request-forgery")
get_detector_findings(severity=["critical", "high"])
```

**For each HIGH/CRITICAL finding:**

1. Validate: `validate_detector_finding(finding_id="H-001")`
2. Read source: `Read("/path/to/file", offset=line-10, limit=30)`
3. Check reachability: `paths_from_entries("FunctionAtLocation")`

**Triage pre-analysis and detector results before moving to manual investigation. If pre-analysis data is unavailable (e.g., no MCP), skip directly to Phase 1 and use grep-based discovery instead.**

---

## Phase 1: Review SSRF Sinks

Pre-analysis `ssrf` and `ssrf_advanced` results already located HTTP client and media processing sinks. Review those results. If pre-analysis is unavailable, or you suspect it missed sinks specific to this codebase, discover them yourself before proceeding.

For each identified sink, investigate:
- Is the URL or any URL component (host, path, query params) derived from user input?
- Is there URL validation before the request is made?
- Can the response be read by the attacker (full SSRF) or is it blind?

---

## Phase 2: Identify URL Sources

For each HTTP sink, identify where the URL comes from:

```
# User-controlled URL parameters
Grep("req\\.(query|params|body)\\.url", type="ts")
Grep("request\\.args\\.get\\(['\"]url", type="py")
Grep("\\$_GET\\[['\"]url", type="php")
Grep("params\\[:url\\]", type="ruby")

# Webhook/callback URLs
Grep("webhook.*url|callback.*url|redirect.*url", glob="**/*", -i=true)
Grep("notify.*url|callback|hook", glob="**/*", -i=true)

# Image/file URL fetching
Grep("image.*url|avatar.*url|icon.*url", glob="**/*", -i=true)
Grep("file.*url|download.*url|fetch.*url", glob="**/*", -i=true)

# PDF/screenshot generation
Grep("pdf.*url|screenshot.*url|render.*url", glob="**/*", -i=true)
Grep("wkhtmltopdf|puppeteer|playwright", glob="**/*")

# Import/export from URL
Grep("import.*url|export.*url|load.*url", glob="**/*", -i=true)
```

---

class FedexUrl extends Value
{
    /**

     */
    private Url $url;
    /**
     * @param Context $context
     * @param Registry $registry
     * @param ScopeConfigInterface $config
     * @param TypeListInterface $cacheTypeList
     * @param AbstractResource|null $resource
     * @param AbstractDb|null $resourceCollection
     * @param Url $url
     * @param array $data
     */
    public function __construct(
        Context $context,
        Registry $registry,
        ScopeConfigInterface $config,
        TypeListInterface $cacheTypeList,
        ?AbstractResource $resource,
        ?AbstractDb $resourceCollection,
        Url $url,
        array $data = []
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context, $registry, $config, $cacheTypeList, $resource, $resourceCollection, $data);
        $this->url = $url;
    }

    /**
     * @inheritDoc
     *
     * @return AbstractModel
     * @throws ValidatorException
     */
    public function beforeSave(): AbstractModel
    {
        $isValid = $this->url->isValid($this->getValue(), ['http', 'https']);
        if ($isValid) {
            // phpcs:ignore Magento2.Functions.DiscouragedFunction
            $host = parse_url((string)$this->getValue(), \PHP_URL_HOST);
        }
        if (!$isValid || (!empty($host) && !preg_match('/(?:.+\.|^)fedex\.com$/i', $host))) {
            throw new ValidatorException(__('Fedex API endpoint URL\'s must use fedex.com'));
        }

        return parent::beforeSave();
    }
}
